extracted.intended_audience: college administrators, science educators, textbook authors, and the scientifically-minded public
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for selecting professors, choosing and adapting textbooks, and designing science education methods appropriate to student age and institutional mission. Emphasizes scientific method, first-hand observation, pedagogical fit, and resistance to ideological censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: University duty to truth / teach knowledge in its most developed forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The first duty of Yale College, as a seat of liberal learning, is to truth, which is to be cordially welcomed from all sources; it is bound to recognize that knowledge is progressive, and to teach it in its most developed and perfected forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universities should prioritize the advancement and presentation of current scientific knowledge over deference to religious or other external pressures. Historical examples (resistance to astronomy and geology) are cited to justify adhering to scientific progress rather than succumbing to theological objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of professor: choose a thoroughgoing, original scholar
rubrics_metrics.description: They sought and obtained a thoroughgoing student of the subject, a man of intellectual force and independence, who would give character to the position, and reflect honor upon the college, by his own original contributions to the science committed to his care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid appointing facile or purely perfunctory instructors; prefer candidates who will advance the discipline and maintain academic liberty even if some governing members are narrow-minded. The governing body should be committed to maintaining the rights of science through its official representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook suitability to students' maturity
rubrics_metrics.description: Professor Sumner adopted Spencer's Study of Sociology to be used by the senior class, consisting of young men from twenty to twenty-three years of age, of mature mind... he adopted the book because it was the only one to be had at all suited to his purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose texts appropriate to the intellectual maturity of the intended class; what is suitable for seniors (20–23) may be inappropriate for younger pupils. Consider whether the work is an introduction for serious inquirers or a primer for beginners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbooks should expose sources of error and bias (e.g., theological bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the students was to gain true ideas ... Nothing could be more pertinent, or necessary, than for them to be put upon their guard against sources of error in considering the subject. One chapter was entitled 'The Theological Bias' and this was considered by some objectionable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is important that educational materials point out common biases and misperceptions (religious or anti-religious) that warp judgment. Omitting such analysis deprives students of necessary critical tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resistance to censorship/expurgation of essential critical content
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a bias from theological influences that is calculated to vitiate or pervert the judgment upon social questions, what could be more important than that it should be pointed out? — Yet the French prepare expurgated editions removing offending parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid removing or sanitizing parts of works that critique influential institutions or beliefs just to placate public or religious sensibilities; while expurgation is presented as a possible compromise, it is implied to be intellectually unsatisfactory and misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of labeling / alignment of title with pedagogical level
rubrics_metrics.description: From this point of view we think the title of the series misleading, and that as a consequence the books are liable to be put to a wrong use. The term primer suggests the lowest grade of elementary school-books — first books for primary classes, or for children beginning to study. The 'Science Primers' are obviously unsuited for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers and adopters must ensure that a book's label (e.g., 'primer') honestly reflects its target audience and pedagogical intent; mislabeling leads to misuse (e.g., teachers using adult-level primers with children).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical method: begin with concrete, first-hand observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Children should begin with the simple, the concrete, the familiar, and be very gradually and very slowly led on to combinations of ideas and the perception of simple relations; the first step should be to direct and guide them in making observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor methods that keep children's natural contact with objects and curiosity (play leading to simple experiments). Avoid early abstraction; use direct observation and activities to build understanding before introducing generalizations or principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature presentation of 'fundamental principles' to beginners
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental principles of the sciences are not 'suited to pupils of an early age,' and cannot be made so by any manner of presentation. The immature mind cannot apprehend them, and though the language may be learned by heart, there will be no real understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not teach high-level abstractions or systematized principles too early; doing so risks rote memorization without comprehension and can 'disturb and paralyze' developing faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on experiments performed by students, not just teacher demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: These experiments must be performed by the teacher in regular order before the class' — criticized as the ancient college way; the pupil should perform experiments himself to be 'brought into immediate contact with Nature herself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design courses and texts so students perform experiments and solve problems themselves. Avoid lecture-and-demonstration-only approaches which fail to cultivate students' investigative faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbooks should cultivate mental self-reliance and original thought
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Inventional Geometry' ... adopts the right method. It will do more to cultivate and strengthen their original powers of thought, more to give them clear ideas and mental self-reliance, than all the other Primers of the series put together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer works that require mental effort and problem solving over those that merely present facts; these better develop independent thinking, even if they are less instantly popular with teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors/editors must account for child psychology and pedagogical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinguished gentlemen who prepared them, and who are masters of the topics, have not given due attention to that very important matter in early education — the minds of children. A man may be deep in physics and profound in astronomy, and yet know very little of the mechanism, growth, and various conditions of the unfolding faculties of the child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing educational materials for early stages, include expertise in child development and elementary pedagogy; subject-matter mastery alone is insufficient for good primers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate role of textbooks in curriculum (facts vs philosophizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: We presume that ... the works to which this was an introduction, or some better book, will be ready for use, and will replace, with its collections of facts, the offensive philosophizings of the 'Study of Sociology.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For introductory courses, especially in schools, favor texts that present factual collections and empirical material rather than heavy philosophical speculation which may be offensive or premature for students; reserve philosophizing for advanced study where students can critique it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local adaptation cautiously as a compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: The French have arranged to prepare an edition of Spencer's 'Education' which the Government may approve, and in which the part dealing with science and classics is omitted. Why not have an edition of 'The Study of Sociology' with the part on the 'theological bias' left out?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While local editions or expurgated adaptations may be used as practical compromises to allow a book into curricula, they are intellectually suspect and may defeat the educational purpose of alerting students to biases; weigh short-term acceptability against long-term pedagogical costs.
